title: Private Credit Worries Result of 'Imbalances,' PIMCO's Karoui
content: PIMCO's Multi-Asset Credit Strategist Lotfi Karoui said concerns building in direct building are a little related to rapid growth. The ongoing exodus from nontraded vehicles, which make up 60% of the sector’s assets, and elevated leverage in their publicly-traded counterparts are key drivers of the credit grader’s revision, according to a report Tuesday. The “disruptive force” presented by artificial intelligence is expected to compound the group’s worries and put it “on defense” in the coming year, Moody’s analysts wrote. An abrupt reversal in the first quarter spurred the first ever net outflow for the sector, Moody’s said. Before artificial intelligence advances set off alarm bells over the durability of software securities, the vehicles had experienced robust net inflows as recently as the third quarter of 2025. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Private Credit Experiencing 'Growing Pains,' SLR Capital Partners' Co-CEO Gross
content: Michael Gross, Co-Founder of SLR Capital Partners said pressure on business development companies are part of private credit's "growing pains." JPMorgan Chase & Co. is restricting some lending to private credit funds after marking down the value loans in their portfolios. At the same time, BDCs — which lend directly to middle-market companies — are seeing elevated redemption requests amid fear of loss related to oversized exposure to software firms disrupted by AI. Besides equity from limited partners and public investors, private credit funds rely on banks for funds. They also raise debt in the investment-grade bond market. (Source: Bloomberg)

­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ ­ [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/6f7648a3-08b6-1c8d-f77d-b57d2467898d.png] Egan-Jones CLO* Summary Report April 2026 *All Egan-Jones ratings in this report are non-NRSRO ratings Still soft issuance levels - at a time when credit yields are reaching recent lows, CLO issuance continues to be weak, perhaps reflecting concerns regarding credit quality. CLOs issued in March decreased from 106 ($48.2B) in 2025 to merely 67 ($27.6B) in 2026<https://egan-jones.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81&id=b13cba0ff9&e=a1880c1820>. Note, these levels were a drastic drop from the Nov. 2024 highs of 127 deals and $54.6B. The 5-year treasuries are moderately low at 397 bps<https://egan-jones.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81&id=b1d633668d&e=a1880c1820> while the ICE US High Yield OAS is also near an annual low at 317bps, well below the high of 461bps in April 2025<https://egan-jones.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81&id=970d987f46&e=a1880c1820>. Regarding CLO credit quality, WARS has improved slightly (see chart below left). The CCC+ or lower rated CLO assets have been stable to slightly down recently as indicated in chart I-D. Regarding asset and tranche coupons, as can be seen in the chart below right both have dipped. Attached is a sample CLO report. [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/06f71d93-8c49-9d80-b1af-1a307e02cce8.jpg] (Adj asset coupon means gross asset coupon minus the asset estimated losses which is assumed 50% of loss given default.) Currently, Egan-Jones tends to have a more positive view of CLO credit quality compared to other credit rating agencies, as demonstrated in the table below. [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/ad5aec63-4d44-ebd9-f820-c7a1219f090c.jpg] I. Deal Key Metrics Summary As of March 2026, Egan-Jones rated 1670 CLO deals. We collected and calculated available deal level, tranche level and asset level key metrics such as deal weighted average rating factor and tranche subordinations, compared with prior period(s) analysis results and summarized highlights below. I-A. Weighted Average Rating Score [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/7b545cd2-ccf9-5807-e5ac-df0c500f9a36.jpg] Egan-Jones collected the weighted average rating score (WARS) of covered CLO deals. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the WARS value were 3607, 3697, and 3832, respectively. (Weighted Average Rating Score is derived from 10-year default rate and used to calculate the weighted average default probability of the portfolio.) I-B. Diversity Score [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/2b4818bc-e4fc-aa6d-e636-2650c8db9a2c.jpg] Egan-Jones collected the Diversity Score (DS) of covered CLO deals. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the DS value were 59, 66, and 72, respectively. (Diversity Score represents the number of independent, identical assets that we can use to mimic the default distribution of the actual portfolio.) I-C. Super Senior Tranches Subordination [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/db679c2f-18fc-2ecd-32fb-1914b43ac68b.jpg] Egan-Jones collected the senior tranches subordination (%) (STS) of covered CLO deals. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the STS value were 32.1, 33.5, and 35.4, respectively. (Tranches Subordination is calculated as (Collateral Value - (Pari-Passu Balance + Senior Balance)) / Collateral Value. Defaulted assets are valued at market value.) I-D. CCC+ or Lower Rating Percentage [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/1f390c15-1021-7c09-59a8-6bee3205b97c.jpg] Egan-Jones collected the CCC+ and Lower Rated Asset Percentage (%) (CLRA) of covered CLO deals. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the CLRA value were 4.9, 6.5, and 9.0, respectively. I-E. CLO Leverage Summary [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/d83229d9-8208-8ca2-0c44-a047f624d619.jpg] Note: Deal balance is the sum of the current balance of all deal tranches; Debt balance is the sum of the current balance of all debt tranches. Egan-Jones reviewed various liability / asset metrics. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the total deal balance to collateral balance (total current tranches balance / current collateral balance) were 93.0%, 96.0%, and 98.0%, respectively. The 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of the debt balance to collateral balance (current non-equity tranches balance / current collateral balance) were 105.0%, 106.0%, and 108.0%, respectively. II. Tranche Key Metrics Summary II-A. Tranche Subordination Analysis [https://mcusercontent.com/f49cef92ca15070cd4ede9f81/images/cd43db59-a89f-366e-c9dc-c0316260558a.jpg] The average subordination levels (defaulted assets are valued at market value) of senior tranches and mezzanine tranches were 36.1% and 13.4%, respectively. Estimated Loss Information Estimated loss is one of the key considerations in EJR's structured finance ratings. In times of stress when economic conditions are deteriorating, default rates and loss severity are more likely to increase relative to a portfolio's initial or base case default and loss severity levels. EJR believes a tranche with higher rating should be able to withstand greater stress and sustain lower losses than a tranche with a lower rating. For example, a tranche with AAA rating should be able to survive the great depression scenario (the highest default and loss severity levels experienced if they were to occur in the future). A 'AA' rated tranche would be more susceptible to an adverse economic impact than the 'AAA' rated tranche but nonetheless should be able to withstand such effects better than a tranche with a lower rating. Allerdings bleiben Zweifel angesichts der Unberechenbarkeit von Donald Trump (79), der gestern noch wüst mit der Auslöschung von Irans Zivilisation gedroht hatte. Es müsse sich erst zeigen, ob die Feuerpause auch halte, so der Tenor unter Analysten. Meine Kollegen Kai Lange und Lutz Reiche geben einen Überblick über die Marktreaktionen und die Faktoren, auf die es jetzt ankommt<https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D>. * Teil der Vereinbarung zwischen den USA und Iran ist auch die Wiedereröffnung der Straße von Hormus. Die für den Welthandel so wichtige Meerenge wird damit zum Testfall: Werden Schiffe tatsächlich wieder ungehindert passieren können? Derzeit sitzen mehr als 2000 Handelsschiffe im Persischen Golf fest, Berichten zufolge wollen die Iraner in nächster Zeit eine Durchfahrtsgebühr von 2 Millionen Dollar pro Schiff <https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D> kassieren. Nicht nur deshalb zeigen sich Reedereien vorerst zurückhaltend und wollen die Lage erst mal prüfen, bevor sie ihre Schiffe am Golf in Gang setzen. * Wie der Ölpreis sinkt heute auch der Preis für Erdgas. Entscheidend für die weitere Entwicklung beim Gas<https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D> sei aber weniger die Wasserstraße von Hormus als vielmehr die Wiederinbetriebnahme des im Krieg beschädigten weltgrößten LNG-Hubs Ras Laffan in Katar, sagen Marktbeobachter. Das Hamburger Pharmaunternehmen konnte seinen Abwärtstrend der vergangenen Jahre damit erst einmal stoppen<https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D>. [separator] Was zum Hören: * Start-up-Acceleratoren sind wichtige Brutstätten für erfolgreiche Neugründungen. Die Firmenschmiede Ewor will in Europa das sein, was das legendäre US-Vorbild Y Combinator im Silicon Valley ist. Wer auf dem alten Kontinent die aussichtsreichen Teams sind und was die neuen KI-Wetten bedeuten, darüber hat mein Kollege Caspar Schlenk mit Ewor-Mitgründer Daniel Dippold (31) im Podcast Finance Forward gesprochen, in den Sie hier hineinhören können.<https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D> [separator] Was Ihnen in Ihrem Unternehmen weiterhelfen könnte: * Künstliche Intelligenz soll uns eigentlich Arbeit abnehmen. Jedoch tritt häufig das Gegenteil ein, wie eine Untersuchung zeigt: KI-Tools lassen die Menschen schneller arbeiten, breitere Aufgabenfelder übernehmen  und mehr Zeit im Job verbringen. Mit der Zunahme der Arbeitsbelastung fühlen sich viele überfordert, gestresst und unter Druck. Wie Sie das verhindern können und auch mit KI fokussiert arbeiten, erfahren Sie hier (HBm+)<https://click.angebote.manager-magazin.de/?%3D%3D>. Die Vorwürfe gegen ihn reichen von unrichtiger Darstellung in den Bilanzen über gewerbsmäßigen Bandenbetrug und Marktmanipulation bis zu besonders schwerer Untreue; dem Ex-Boss des Zahlungsdienstleisters drohen bis zu 15 Jahre Gefängnis. Doch vor Gericht inszeniert sich Braun hartnäckig als Opfer: Er habe keinerlei Kenntnisse von Fälschungen oder Veruntreuungen, er selbst sei ausgetrickst worden, so seine Darstellung. Zur Aufklärung trug der Ex-Chef damit kaum bei, so meine Kollegin Katharina Slodczyk, die den Prozess eng verfolgt hat. Brauns Verteidigungsstrategie droht zu scheitern  und eine Verurteilung rückt womöglich näher. AI agents in retail investing People do not like to lose money on stocks. Sometimes a stock goes down, and people who own it sell it to avoid losing more money, so it goes down more. This behavior is to some extent predictable, so there are circumstances in which you might think<https://links.message.bloomberg.com/s/c/Bg376sF7KW8UbFNHyimAWoDl_TThQj_vtykDNNz7WLE27Lvvmpn6lfGMkZxo5oRGOcZHyQRXXg3UfKzyT0mGJeYjSSIi7mIx7opIarRHroMAhtfn_-DCKIsROc6YZEnaOpwC-YLnZQEQlTE9X0VpLZblfI2nQVC_jLzY6uvKJJIQgQdlMR6aYHP0mzewO3fQMJ1BQZJJ5Vfd3moEAJJBZinEwvirzikm0BrLBVLl4rInRFCO7EiE9ieCH8meIiD9UIGTgbfuefNE9wNlwOC-yys6Ku1PM_xgDQN4FFmt7tzK2ArLtEMXUbgAppV6Fl7E5vM0Nd49pxNl4_MIcLnUd3BsViWEBC1MbXtJRZGHGPJGUorYJBb8QRb0nw/yVZV_n9eNtu-wOJIGQbhHl9bvlxREMX0/19> if this stock goes below $50, it will probably keep going down to $45. You might think that as a pure matter of investor psychology: If the stock goes below $50, a lot of people who bought it at $50 will have losses and panic and hit the sell button, driving it down more. You might have a slightly different theory. Because people do not like to lose money on stocks, and are not monitoring their stocks constantly, they might use stop-loss orders<https://links.message.bloomberg.com/s/c/C1N9UoeNt3Dbz8ysDHEWuZ79OcQKFGxoEZAbBPgtjtcO43_18Xtyj1Sb-oMtzImsz8RkLwF_gl4hPmqq8BctnWe8D_66cbaFuRGrIYq7FrLjFRCGrdMONBX8vnsAQMkch2amPU9sFyrXmqjly6avxU5KqTozEl2CA04bwetLm1923LQhFMfC8SY5NOCXI9hmAo4e82HBy_g0sNQQDR9r_WkfOgzZJdFIBq7Ct43Y2es08XrGjgoHYeQv81h2Al214npwPHKVLHFyib5wrokeK_8wx4I2_HoPUsw7vss8fP-cDO26wu4OFuF4i2Y6YZcqPLReOG3S2A66Hy71KSLxCmn7VGgmqo9lDZUxoZ3Q3vxIC86LbJ591d1CEw/C3YlrfZMgsFv9GJYN5C82R-sabFGIxiM/19>, where they tell their broker if this stock goes below $50, sell it immediately. Intuitively, people who do this are more likely to use round numbers like $50 than, like, if this stock goes below $51.37, sell it, so there is some clustering of stop-loss orders; there are more of them at some numbers than at others. In a sense, the previous two paragraphs express the same idea: They both say people have irrational biases that make them anchor on round numbers and fear losses, so if the stock falls to $50 there will be further irrational selling driving it down to $45. The difference is the mechanism: In the first paragraph, the stock hits $50 and then people decide to sell; in the second paragraph, people plan ahead to sell if the stock hits $50, and automate that selling. But the second paragraph feels more real, more predictable: I know there are stop orders to sell at $50, so if the stock falls below $50 it will keep going down has a bit more science to it than I think people will panic at $50 and sell more. This point might generalize. Like: 1. Everything that happens in financial markets reflects, in some way, investor psychology. If you have a good aggregate sense of how investors think about stuff, and stuff happens, then you can predict whether asset prices will go up or down. But this is very hard and somewhat fuzzy, and if you said I have perfect insight into how investors think so give me money to start a hedge fund, people might not believe you. The dispersion trade is, classically, a bet on stereotypical behavior by investors: They like to buy index options to hedge broad market risk, and they like to sell single-stock options for income. Therefore index options trade at a premium and single-stock options trade at a discount, and you can manufacture index options out of single-stock options to capture that spread. [3] But it is also a fundamental bet on correlation. If individual stocks are volatile but uncorrelated, then their volatility will cancel each other out: Some stocks will go up 2%, some will go down 1.5%, and the overall stock index will go up 0.5%. Index volatility will be lower than single-stock volatility, and a strategy of buying single-stock options and selling index options will make a lot of money. [4] If individual stocks all move together, then theyll all go up 2% today and down 1.5% tomorrow, the overall index will go up 2% today and down 1.5% tomorrow, index volatility will be high and youll lose money on the dispersion trade. [5] As we discussed last month, a reasonable fundamental story in February was something like the rise of artificial intelligence is going to create huge winners and huge losers, so there will be a lot of dispersion among stocks. And February was a great month for the dispersion trade. title: Banks Selling $3 Billion Debt for Meta’s Prometheus Data Center
content: A group of banks including Natixis SA, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. and Societe Generale SA have started selling $3 billion of loans for a data center in Ohio backed by Meta Platforms Inc., the latest deal supporting the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
